argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only as a caveated certification narrative, not as a clean or unconditional one. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and passing general support, latency, and rollback checks support launch readiness. The same admissible record also establishes that Spanish billing-ticket triage is a named deployment context with missing eval coverage and unknown risk status, so the certification defense is supportable only if the audit packet and model card frame that gap as an unresolved limitation rather than as passed coverage. On that basis, the issue is not whether certification is categorically unsupported; it is whether the record should be treated as compliant only with the required disclosure caveat.
claims_about_business_cost: No escalation is necessary if the auditor treats this as caveated compliance and requires the packet to reflect the disclosed gap. That approach preserves the supported certification path while avoiding the larger launch delay that would come from treating operational-readiness evidence as irrelevant or demanding a clean-certification showing the record does not support.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not require treating missing named-context eval coverage as passed, and it does not allow clean certification on general operational evidence alone. It does allow launch-readiness evidence to support certification when material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts are disclosed. The admissible evidence therefore supports a narrowed policy reading: certification is defensible if and only if the record is conditioned on explicit disclosure of the Spanish billing-ticket evaluation gap and unknown limitation status.
concessions: The current admissible record does not prove that the final model-card disclosure has already been completed.
The record does not support any claim of clean certification with no deployment limitation.
Missing Spanish billing-ticket evals cannot be treated as effectively passed merely because no completed test failed.
